what: This tracking stock represents Liberty Media's Formula One business. Formula One owns the commercial rights to the world championship: it sells the television rights, race hosting fees and trackside sponsorship for every grand prix.
customers: Broadcasters and streaming services, race promoters and governments hosting races, sponsors, and fans buying tickets and hospitality.
money: fees paid by circuits and governments to host a grand prix
trackside and title sponsorship, hospitality and licensing
moat: A sport with no substitute: there is one Formula One world championship, and the teams, circuits and audience are all contracted to it.
risks: Race hosting fees depend on governments willing to subsidise events
Media rights are renegotiated in large blocks, so a weak renewal matters for years
The tracking stock structure complicates ownership
opportunities: Revenue grew about 23% last year and about 12% a year over three years
American interest in the sport has risen sharply, which lifts US media and sponsorship value
New races and expanded calendars add hosting fees
watch: Media rights renewals and the number of races on the calendar.
